subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw cache low-risk exec auto-reviewer `allow-once` verdicts per reviewer instance, and what key/scope is approved for that security boundary?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the repair changes approval caching semantics in a security-sensitive exec path and two open PRs propose overlapping implementations.

options.title: Approve bounded full-input memo
options.body: Cache only low-risk `allow-once` results per reviewer instance using the full serialized reviewer input, with tests proving duplicate hits and changed-context misses.

options.title: Keep fresh completions
options.body: Reject memoization if maintainers want every approval miss to receive an independent model review despite the extra billing.

options.title: Request a narrower design
options.body: Hold both PRs until a maintainer specifies a different key, cache lifetime, or verdict set for the reviewer memo.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded full-input memo
recommendation.body: Cache only low-risk `allow-once` results per reviewer instance using the full serialized reviewer input, with tests proving duplicate hits and changed-context misses.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current-main history owner for the reviewer and both host call sites most directly affected by the cache boundary.
